Removes obsolete bio handling code (bio_setup_sector, bio_advance) now unnecessary after loop removal, replacing it with direct size assignment, cleaning up dm driver.
Adds a guest_cpu field to perf thread structures and populates it from hypervisor (QEMU) VCPU information, enabling perf to identify which guest CPU a host thread corresponds to.
The patch adds the PnP ID "LEN040f" to the Synaptics driver’s device list, enabling InterTouch (rmi4) support for ThinkPad P1 Gen 3, which was previously disabled.

Adds a hardware workaround Wa_16013835468 for Tiger Lake/DG1 GPUs: introduces helper to select register bits per pipe, passes CRTC state to PSR enable, sets/clears a chicken register when vblank exceeds vtotal, and updates register definitions.

The patch adds the const qualifier to many initialization tables and related pointer parameters in the rtl8xxxu driver, turning read‑only data into true constants and updating function signatures accordingly.

Updates the mt8195 pinctrl devicetree binding YAML, adding a wrapping node for pin configuration groups, reorganizing schema with patternProperties, and providing new examples, thereby improving documentation clarity.

The commit adds a runtime check for Xilinx hardware via firmware API, updates Kconfig dependency, and switches to module_platform_driver, preventing the SHA3 driver from loading on unsupported platforms and fixing crashes.
Refactors the qla2xxx EDIF BSG interface by adding a version field to structures, inserting version checks, and removing unused fields and interfaces, preparing for future enhancements.
The commit fixes a misspelled word in a comment of opa_vnic.h, changing "structrue" to "structure". It only modifies documentation, leaving code behavior unchanged.

The commit introduces device‑tree bindings for the Qualcomm SM6350 camera clock controller, adding a YAML schema and a header with clock and GDSC identifiers, enabling kernel support for this hardware.
The commit changes rtl8xxxu_print_chipinfo to compute the chip cut character directly, supporting values 0‑15 (A‑P) instead of a limited switch, thus eliminating "unknown" for valid cuts.

The patch changes workqueue early init to fetch the housekeeping cpumask for HK_FLAG_WQ separately and then intersect it with HK_FLAG_DOMAIN, removing the combined flag variable. This prepares each HK_FLAG_* to be handled independently for future cpuset support.
The commit updates the MAINTAINERS file, changing John Garry's email address from a Huawei domain to an Oracle domain. No code or functional changes are introduced.
Removes the .owner field from the platform driver definition because the core automatically sets it, eliminating a platform_no_drv_owner.cocci warning.
Adds power-management support to the Microchip PCI1XXXX SPI driver by implementing suspend/resume callbacks, storing and restoring hardware configuration, and registering the driver’s pm ops.

The patch changes the baud‑rate handling in the FTDI USB‑serial driver: it replaces the post‑switch fallback check with a default case that logs unsupported rates and falls back to 9600, correcting the long‑standing mis‑mapping of 300 bps.

Adds support for PERF_SAMPLE_DATA_SRC in AMD IBS events by converting IBS raw data into perf_mem_data_src structures, introduces helper functions, updates parsing and offset handling, enabling tools to receive detailed memory access information.
Adds a vfree(orom_data) on error path in ice_get_orom_civd_data() to prevent a memory leak when ice_read_flash_module fails.

Adds new BPF self‑tests that verify rejection of read‑only memory passed to global functions and kfuncs, introduces test program test_global_func17.c, and updates test harness to run two variants, expanding test coverage.

The commit introduces a sysfs "label" attribute for ChromeOS EC sensors, mapping known sensor locations to human‑readable labels, and removes the previous non‑standard "location" attribute and related code.
The commit corrects the fsl,clk-source property in the LX2160A device tree from <0> to /bits/ 8 <0>, matching its uint8 type and removing a warning about property length.
Adds Roman Gushchin as a co‑maintainer for the memory controller subsystem by inserting his entry into the MAINTAINERS file.

The patch removes the unused iscsi_create_conn function and replaces its use with iscsi_alloc_conn followed by iscsi_add_conn after the connection's data is initialized, preventing a NULL pointer dereference when userspace accesses sysfs attributes.
The patch changes the cast of of_device_get_match_data() from enum mxcmci_type to uintptr_t to silence a clang warning about casting a void pointer to a smaller integer type.
Adds bitrate_const to can_changelink() validation, correcting the omission that prevented configuring fixed‑bitrate CAN devices without a no‑op do_set_bittiming callback.
Adds cleanup of stream_ctx_array on allocation failure in xhci_alloc_stream_info, calling xhci_free_stream_ctx to prevent a memory leak.
Adds NULL checks after ioremap calls in the ray_cs driver and jumps to error handling to avoid dereferencing NULL pointers.
The patch changes vsock_connect to use mod_delayed_work instead of schedule_delayed_work and adds a sock_put when the work was already pending, eliminating a reference‑count leak reported by syzbot.
The commit replaces the legacy i2c-at91 text binding with a new Device Tree JSON schema YAML file, adding the schema and removing the old .txt documentation.
Moves the LCOUNT mask constant from inline GENMASK usage to a named macro in sdw_intel.h, updating references in intel.c and intel_init.c to use the macro.
The patch modifies map_block() to reset handle and size, call get_hw_block_id(), and return early on error, ensuring no valid handle is returned when the hardware block ID lookup fails.
The patch corrects the WARN_ON condition in ice_vsi_rebuild to also test the VF pointer, preventing a kernel warning and crash when resetting virtual functions.
The patch deletes the fallback attempt to set a 32‑bit DMA mask after a 64‑bit mask call, because the 64‑bit call never fails when dev->dma_mask is set. This removes dead code in two driver files.

Adds a call to set_counter_value in armada_37xx_wdt_set_timeout so the hardware watchdog counter is updated when the timeout is changed via ioctl, fixing the failure where the timeout was not applied.
The commit removes the redundant is_enabled field and its related enable/disable/is_enabled functions from the ux500 PRCMU clock driver, using the core's existing enable count.

Reorganizes XIP‑related #ifdef macros in arch/riscv/mm/init.c, moving pt_ops macro next to other XIP definitions, grouping related macros, and removing redundant #ifdef blocks while adding an extern declaration.

The patch introduces a device counter and mutex to track registered target devices, allowing the db_root configuration to be changed only when no devices are present, fixing the previous blanket restriction.

Adds error‑path cleanup for legacy kprobe events in libbpf: when determining the kprobe type or opening the perf event fails, the newly created kprobe_event is removed, fixing the -EBUSY issue when livepatch and kprobe coexist.
Adds MediaTek mt8186 SCP support to the remoteproc driver by defining new registers, implementing a before‑load routine, providing an of_data structure, and registering the compatible device.

Adds module parameters to the speakup_dummy driver, allowing default driver variables to be set at boot by converting the var array to an indexed enum and exposing each variable's default_val via module_param_named.
Adds a deprecated "riscv,clint0" compatible string to the sifive,clint DT binding to stop dt-validate errors for QEMU-generated DTBs.

The patch modifies swiotlb_max_mapping_size() to subtract alignment padding derived from the device's minimum alignment mask, ensuring the reported max DMA mapping size respects slot alignment and fixing boot failures on Hyper‑V VMs with forced swiotlb.

Switches command buffer handling to the unified memory manager, removing the legacy cb_mgr structures and related functions, updating all callers to use hl_mem_mgr APIs, and cleaning up associated code.
Modifies vmbus_request_addr to return VMBUS_RQST_ERROR for a zero transaction ID, preventing a NULL dereference in netvsc_send_completion, and clarifies comments about ID 0 reservation.

The patch adds fields to the source buffer, implements a function to detect resolution/pixfmt changes, updates capture queue parameters, and integrates this logic into the JPEG parser, enabling dynamic resolution handling.
Replace memcpy with copy_map_value in bpf_selem_alloc to avoid copying the spin‑lock field of map values, ensuring the lock remains zeroed as allocated.

The patch fixes a race where multiple ADD_ADDR options could overwrite the stored remote address after releasing the PM lock, by caching the address earlier, handling missing port values, and ensuring the echoed address matches the received one.
The commit separates Zynq A05 DDR controller from the generic Synopsys DDRC ECC binding, updates the Synopsys schema, adds a new binding file for Zynq A05, and updates MAINTAINERS accordingly.
Removes the "status = \"okay\"" line from the i2s1 node in the Rock Pi 4 device tree, disabling the I2S1 controller so its pins can function as GPIO, aligning with the hardware's default behavior.
The patch adds two clock definitions (adc_adclk, adc_pclk) and two reset definitions (ADC_PRESETN, ADC_ADRST_N) for the ADC block in the Renesas r9a07g043 CPG driver.
The patch deletes the declaration and assignment of the variable 'mdss' in msm_drv.c because the code that used it was removed, eliminating a clang -Wunused-but-set-variable warning.
Adds skb drop reason enums and tracing, updates tcp_v4_rcv to set and pass a drop reason to kfree_skb_reason, improving diagnostics without changing packet handling logic.
Removes now‑unnecessary comment and overflow‑check in highmem_dirtyable_memory after earlier fix ensures x cannot be negative, simplifying the function.

Updates MAINTAINERS to reference the new YAML binding files for Mediatek JPEG driver, fixing a broken reference that caused get_maintainer.pl to report an error and generalizing the entry for both decoder and encoder.

The patch replaces the old xfs_buf_incore() function with a new API that returns an error code and outputs the buffer via a pointer, adds XBF_INCORE flag, updates callers to handle errors, and removes the obsolete wrapper, making buffer handling consistent across XFS.
The patch fixes the DSC slice calculation in the AMD DRM driver by moving the feasibility check before zeroing min slices, ensuring both min and max slices must fit the pixel clock.
Adds clock and reset definitions for PWM channels 8‑14 in the Renesas r9a09g011 CPG driver, exposing them to Linux and marking the APB clock as critical.

The patch corrects FDMA MTU handling by reading the hardware MTU, adding space for skb_shared_info and VLAN headers, and fixing the register write on error, ensuring proper page order calculation and preventing allocation failures when MTU changes.

Adds support for dumping the non‑protected nVHE hypervisor stacktrace from EL1 by introducing a stacktrace info struct and functions that record stack base, overflow base, FP and PC, and invoking them on panic.
Corrects a typo in the driver’s error log, changing "failed to register PMC" to "failed to register PCM".
The patch adds a line in amdgpu_vkms_sw_init to set fb_modifiers_not_supported = true, addressing GDM3 start failures on virtual displays caused by missing modifier support in vkms.
The commit corrects the Chinese translation of the devicetree usage-model documentation, keeping the term 'machine_desc' untranslated by adjusting a few lines in the .rst file.
Adds internal helper functions to read block data and verify block register presence, avoiding errors with PEC, by integrating status checks and fault clearing.
Replaces the multiline macro vt6655_mac_word_reg_bits_off with an equivalent static function, updates the header, and removes the macro definition to satisfy checkpatch requirements.
The commit adjusts the sysfs-fs-erofs ABI documentation to correct indentation and block‑quote formatting, eliminating Sphinx warnings during HTML doc generation.
Adds fields and code to correctly initialize BA CAM for 8852c (bacam_v1) chips, fixing wrong H2C content and providing dynamic entry setup.
Adjusts indentation in dcn32_hwseq.c to resolve a smatch warning; no functional code changes.

The patch introduces separate TX and RX FIFO flush bits, adds a flag to indicate shared flush behavior, and updates startup logic to flush the appropriate FIFO before activation, fixing the bug where RX FIFO was never flushed on SoCs with independent bits.
Enables the QUP and GPI DMA nodes in the sm6350 device tree by setting their status to "okay", preparing the platform for future I2C support.
Adds PCI device IDs for Intel Raptor Lake PCH‑S LPSS variants to the intel‑lpss driver, enabling the kernel to recognize and bind these new devices.
Removes a duplicated word 'to' from a comment in drivers/crypto/n2_core.c, cleaning up documentation without changing code behavior.
Adds Accuphase DAC-60 USB ID to the DSD format quirk list, enabling native DSD playback for that device.
Adds full support for the VCN 4.0 IP block, including firmware handling, initialization, power/clock gating, ring management, and interrupt handling in the AMDGPU driver.
Adds EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL lines for decoder power‑management functions so they are visible when the driver is built as a module, enabling other components to call them.
Adds READ_ONCE() around accesses to net->ipv4.sysctl_igmp_qrv in IGMP and AMT code to eliminate concurrent read/write races, fixing a data‑race bug.

The patch introduces a local boolean variable rx_timeout that stores the result of the UART IIR RX timeout check, then uses it in the subsequent conditional. No functional behavior changes, only refactoring for clarity.
Adds proper error handling for nvmem_device_find returns and safe release of nvmem devices, fixing crashes caused by dereferencing error pointers.

The patch renames the macro ID_AA64MMFR2_EL1_LVA_SHIFT to ID_AA64MMFR2_EL1_VARange_SHIFT in several ARM64 files, updating all references to align with the official DDI0487H.a naming. No functional behavior changes.
The patch updates comments and formatting in rzg2l_thermal.c: replaces a vague macro comment, corrects a typo, and moves block comments to separate lines per coding style.
The patch removes a duplicated 'the' in a comment of vas.c, fixing a typo and improving comment clarity.
The commit deletes the unused variable `cnt` from recv_func in the r8188eu driver, simplifying the pending‑frame loop without altering runtime behavior.

The patch replaces a busy‑wait loop that could spin forever when the hardware semaphore cannot be obtained (e.g., after surprise removal) with a check that logs an error and aborts the release, thus eliminating the infinite loop.

Moves maybe_wait_bpf_programs() out of the per‑element loop in generic_map_delete_batch() to after the loop, as the RCU barrier is only needed before returning to userspace, reducing unnecessary synchronization.

The patch refactors the KVM state_test self‑test to stop using a hard‑coded VCPU_ID, creates the VM with vm_create_with_one_vcpu, passes a struct kvm_vcpu pointer, and switches to vcpu_run, simplifying the test code.
Replaces CONFIG_PM_SLEEP #ifdef guards with pm_sleep_ptr() and DEFINE_SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS in vf610 DAC driver, simplifying compile‑time handling of power‑management code.

The commit updates the header comment of tools/testing/radix-tree/maple.c, changing the description line and extending the copyright notice from 2018 to 2018‑2022 and adding an Author line. No code behavior is altered.
The patch drops the unused i2c_device_id argument from rc5t583_i2c_probe and registers the driver with the newer .probe_new callback, modernizing the driver to the current I2C driver API.
The patch adds early NULL returns in vchiq_get_state when the remote pointer is missing or not initialized, and restructures the logic for clearer flow and logging.

The patch moves efi32_pe_entry into the .text section, replaces absolute relocations with relative offsets, and adjusts address calculations, enabling the function to be extracted to a separate compilation unit later.
The patch relocates two constant arrays defining CEC register offsets from the public header to the CEC driver source file, eliminating unused-variable warnings when the CEC feature is disabled.
Adds the CLK_OPS_PARENT_ENABLE flag to pixel and byte clock sources in the SM6350 display clock driver so that the parent clock is enabled before rate changes, fixing failures in set_rate.
The patch renames the driver’s master/slave mode flag to provider_mode and updates the ASoC DAI format handling to use the newer CLOCK_PROVIDER masks, adjusting related logic and error messages.
Adds a command‑specific flag to gsi_channel_data_valid and runtime checks for direction, TLV count limits and TRE size, ensuring IPA command channels are correctly configured.

The patch corrects the layout of the packed result_data_desc struct by replacing mixed‑type fields with uniform 32‑bit bit‑fields, eliminating unintended padding that broke zero‑initialisation and size calculations.
Adds a read‑back of VCAP filter counters before moving a filter, preventing stale hit counts from being written to hardware and correcting wrong statistics.
The commit deletes a conditional IS_SWAPFILE macro definition in fs/nfs/file.c because the macro is always defined elsewhere, removing dead code.

The patch corrects the regulator bypass enable check by using the .is_enabled() operation instead of .enable, which cannot determine current state, and removes an unused variable, ensuring proper error handling when the regulator is already enabled.

Adds a completed_id field to gsi transaction tracking, updates move/complete/polled logic to maintain this ID, and removes temporary warnings, improving internal state tracking and consistency checks.
The commit deletes the now‑unused tstamp pointer from mlx5e_txqsq and removes related assignments in the driver, cleaning up dead code after a prior PTP migration.
The patch modifies i2c read functions to handle negative i2c errors separately, avoiding a misleading "Invalid frame length" error message and returning the original error code.
The commit updates the ath11k device‑tree binding documentation to include qcom,smem‑states and qcom,smem‑state‑names properties, enabling Wake on Wireless support for the WCN6750 chipset.

The patch adds a local macro AGGREGATOR_MAX_GPIOS (512) and replaces all uses of ARCH_NR_GPIOS in the gpio‑aggregator driver for bitmap allocation, parsing, and iteration, removing reliance on the system‑wide GPIO count.
The patch reformats block comments in rtw_cmd.c to use the standard /* ... */ style without extra asterisks, aligning with drivers/net coding conventions.
Adds a new Device Tree binding YAML file for the Renesas RZ/G2L interrupt controller, defining compatible strings, interrupt cells, registers, clocks, power domains, resets, and an example node.
The commit changes the return type of PS_RDY_CHECK from u8 to bool, reflecting that the function returns true/false, improving type correctness.
Adds a check in gfs2_glock_dq to skip dequeuing when a GL_ASYNC holder was already removed after a failed async lock, fixing a race condition.
The patch removes the driver‑specific yesno() helper and replaces its uses with the kernel‑wide str_yes_no() from string_helpers.h, adding the appropriate header.
The patch deletes an assignment that accessed the slot_data array with an invalid slot index when JPEG parsing fails, preventing out‑of‑bounds access and the resulting kernel panic.
Adds two compatible strings for DH electronics i.MX8M Plus DHCOM and PDK2 boards to the arm/fsl.yaml devicetree binding file, updating documentation.
The patch stores the original end address (last) before the translation loop and passes it unchanged to vhost_iotlb_itree_first, fixing incorrect range handling during descriptor translation.
Adds a guard (i > 0) before accessing args[i-1] in next_arg, preventing out‑of‑bounds read that caused a kernel page fault when parsing quoted arguments.
Reorders functions and variables in the via686a hwmon driver to eliminate unnecessary forward declarations, moving static definitions earlier; no functional changes.
The patch adds checks to skip frequency QoS updates when the ACPI _PPC value hasn't changed and aligns init handling with a default "no limit" QoS value, improving efficiency and consistency.
The commit deletes the arm64 entry from scripts/head-object-list.txt, removing the previous forced link order for head.o because the linker script already places the required header correctly.

The patch adds RAS‑DES register definitions, introduces a ras_des_cap field, discovers the capability offset at runtime, and replaces hard‑coded offsets in the Tegra194 driver with the discovered value.
Adds be_pause counter and fe_pause flag to backend PCM handling, changing STOP to PAUSE when all streams are paused, improving resource management for PAUSE_RELEASE transitions.

Adds a configurable feature to track and display modules that taint the kernel when they are unloaded, including new Kconfig option, Makefile entry, data structures, helper functions, and printing logic.
Adds a lockdown check to the /proc/powerpc/ofdt write path, preventing untrusted device‑tree modifications when kernel lockdown is active; also introduces LOCKDOWN_DEVICE_TREE enum and description.
Adds .legacy_dai_naming = 1 to ADI AXI I2S and AXI SPDIF component drivers, switching them to legacy DAI naming mode required by the new naming scheme.
Replaces kzalloc(sizeof(*config) * 4) with kcalloc(4, sizeof(*config)) to allocate an array, adding overflow checks and using the appropriate allocator.
The patch removes the unused regs pointer from coredump_params, replacing its use with task_pt_regs(current) in ELF core dump handling, and deletes the struct member, simplifying the code.
Adds a missing dma_release_channel() call in emac_probe() error handling to release the DMA channel allocated earlier, fixing a resource leak.

The patch changes several Btrfs ioctl helper functions to accept a struct inode pointer directly instead of a struct file, removing repeated file_inode() calls. Call sites are updated accordingly, and the send ioctl signature is adjusted. This refactors the code for reuse of the already‑extracted inode.
The patch replaces a manual lookup of ACPI device match data with the generic device_get_match_data() call and marks the methods pointer as const, removing redundant code.
Adds rdev_mdlock_deref helper for safe RCU dereference under mddev_lock, replaces direct dereferences with it, adds lockdep assertion, and removes sparse warnings.

Implements kernel‑side handling of GTP Echo Request messages by generating Echo Responses for GTPv0 and GTPv1‑U, adds restart‑counter attribute and related netlink configuration, and introduces helper structures and routing logic. Enables GTP devices created via ip link to comply with the GTP spec without a userspace daemon.
Adds a bt_dev_name macro that checks for NULL hdev and updates bt_dev_* logging macros to use it, preventing dereference of a NULL pointer and fixing a kernel crash.
The patch replaces cpumask_next* calls with cpumask_first* equivalents, adds cpumask_first_zero() implementation, and updates several drivers and core code to use the new helpers.
Marks the Clevo mail LED driver as BROKEN in Kconfig and corrects wording, preventing the driver from being built until the problematic brightness‑based blink interface is fixed.
The patch adds a line that sets the BSS pointer to NULL when the lookup returns an error, preventing later code from attempting to free an error pointer.
Adds missing bit definitions and conditional logic so Aquantia PHY advertises 2.5G/5G only when those speeds are requested, correcting wrong default advertising.
Adds missing rcu_read_lock/unlock and reference handling in bond_ethtool_get_ts_info to protect against calls via setsockopt, fixing a kernel crash reported by syzbot.
Adds extra dev_info messages to log SSP, DMIC and GPIO quirks in the sof_es8336 driver, extending existing logging.
The patch renames the debug‑message fields maxpctksize and maxpcktsize to the correct wMaxPacketSize in f_uac2.c, fixing inconsistent spelling without altering functionality.
The commit extends perf's JSON conversion to include tracepoint fields by iterating over event format fields and printing them into the JSON output.
Corrects misspelled words in warning and debug messages in NVMe authentication code, improving log readability.
The commit corrects a duplicated word 'the the' to 'the' in two comment lines (amdgpu_fence.c and atombios.h), improving comment clarity without changing any code behavior.

The patch refactors conv_uni_to_pc in consolemap.c, extracting the page directory pointer, adding explicit NULL checks, splitting a complex conditional into simpler steps, and removing an extraneous newline, improving code readability without changing behavior.
Adds a new maintainer entry for the Allwinner A31 MIPI CSI-2 bridge driver in the MAINTAINERS file, listing Paul Kocialkowski and linking to the driver source and DT bindings.
Adds device‑specific entries for two Chicony EasyCamera models, mapping them to a limited power‑line control handler to work around their broken implementation.
The patch removes the obsolete odm_2to1_policy_applied flag and its comparison, fixing a false change detection that caused unnecessary stream reprogramming and intermittent black screens on HDMI.
Removes the '@0' unit address from panel endpoint nodes in am335x device tree files, because endpoint nodes must not have a unit address, fixing the 'reg' required property error.
The patch replaces drm_mode_copy with drm_mode_init when initializing an on‑stack drm_mode struct, ensuring the list head is cleared and avoiding stack garbage.

The patch replaces a direct uncore register write (intel_uncore_rmw) with the higher‑level intel_de_rmw accessor in the display power initialization, removing low‑level hardware access from display code.
Adds runtime checks when enumerating VCN and SDMA instances, ensuring the count does not exceed driver‑defined maximums; logs an error if firmware reports excess instances.

Adds a function to sort the amode31 exception table early in startup_init and removes the previous call from trap_init, ensuring the table is sorted before the early program‑check handler runs, thus preventing missed entries.

The commit removes the driver’s reset_resume callback for the xpad wireless controller, letting the USB core rebind the device after a suspend/resume cycle, which prevents the URB hang that broke LED and force‑feedback functionality.
Changes fb_modesetting_disabled in fb.h to a static inline function, eliminating multiple definition linker errors when the header is included in multiple objects.

The commit adds Clause‑45 MDIO PHY management to the lan743x driver: defines MMD access constants, implements helper functions for Clause‑45 reads/writes, updates the MDIO bus to advertise C45 capability, and switches the bus callbacks accordingly.
Adds a new stub header tools/include/linux/pfn.h with PFN macros for testing, introducing new code without fixing bugs or improving existing code.

The patch stops calling acpi_video_set_dmi_backlight_type() in the Toshiba ACPI driver, removes related dead code, and adds DMI entries in video_detect to force the vendor backlight driver for two Toshiba models, eliminating a race where the acpi_video device briefly appears then disappears.
The patch removes the driver code that queries the 'dtim_assoc' IOVAR after roaming, which always failed and spammed the console, so the driver no longer attempts to get TIM info from firmware.
Replace BUG_ON checks with WARN_ON_ONCE in do_notify_parent to avoid kernel panic during debugging, allowing continuation while still logging unexpected conditions.
Removes three redundant boolean initializations (bPacketMatchBSSID, bPacketToSelf, bPacketBeacon) in update_recvframe_phyinfo_88e of the r8188eu driver, as they are set later before use.

The patch modifies shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp to use shmem_get_folio_gfp, handling folios directly, unlocking with folio_unlock, converting to a page via folio_file_page, and removing extra compound_head() calls, thus streamlining the code.
Adds validation for NTFS BOOT sectors_per_clusters, returning -EINVAL for out‑of‑range values and handling the error in init, preventing shift‑out‑of‑bounds UBSAN crash.

The patch modifies RISC‑V KASAN early initialization to use pfn_pte/virt_to_pfn instead of mk_pte/virt_to_page, preventing a pfn_to_page call that dereferences a null mem_section when sparsemem is enabled without vmemmap, thereby fixing a boot‑time crash.
The patch reuses a scatter‑gather table cache for normal S/G paths, enlarges the cached buffer size, and replaces per‑packet allocations with get/recycle helpers, adding a macro for max entries.
The commit updates the maintainer entry for Krzysztof Kozlowski in the MAINTAINERS file, replacing his old canonical.com email with his kernel.org address.
Adds a 'skip' enum value to the qcom,gsi-loader property in the IPA devicetree binding, documenting that firmware loading can be omitted when already loaded.

The commit changes the SDM630 device tree to describe the TCSR mutex as a memory‑mapped hwlock instead of a syscon, adding the required reg property and #hwlock-cells, thereby satisfying DT schema checks.
The patch corrects interrupt handling on PowerPC/64s by fixing a branch that caused loss of pending soft‑masked IRQs and adds logic to clear the HARD_DIS flag, with explanatory comments.
Adds an io_master helper, removes a duplicate definition, and changes CPU hotpluggable flag logic so IO master CPUs are not marked hotpluggable, preventing sysfs control file creation.
Deletes the unused variable 'last' and its assignment in remove_siblinginfo() of arch/ia64/kernel/smpboot.c, eliminating dead code without changing runtime behavior.

Updates the fp selftest Makefile to use TEST_GEN_PROGS_EXTENDED for generated programs, moving appropriate binaries from TEST_PROGS_EXTENDED and keeping script-based stress tests there, adjusting the all target accordingly.
Adds rollback of font data, dimensions, and userfont state when vc_resize fails, restoring previous values to prevent inconsistent console state, addressing a syzbot‑reported page fault bug.
Adds a 'power-domains' property to the MediaTek vcodec encoder device-tree binding documentation, enabling the encoder node to reference a power domain.
Adds a case to is_info_event to treat a range of power/thermal events as informational, lowering their log level to info because they do not indicate errors.
Updates the Hirschmann Hellcreek device tree binding YAML to use an absolute $ref path (/schemas/leds/common.yaml#) instead of a relative one, aligning with preferred documentation practice.
Adds EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL for mt6358 driver functions to resolve undefined symbol errors when the codec is built as a module.
Reorders bits in dp_128b_132b_supported_lttpr_link_rates struct to follow DP2.0 spec, moving UHBR13_5 after UHBR20.
Adds an early‑return in slim_rx_mux_put to skip updating when the new value equals the current one, preventing unnecessary change notifications that caused spurious events in the wcd9335 ASoC driver.

The patch moves spin_lock_irqsave(&card->lock, flags) to enclose accesses of card->local_node and bm_retries in fw_core_handle_bus_reset, and removes internal locking from fw_destroy_nodes, adding a comment that the function must be called with card->lock held. This ensures those fields are always accessed while holding the lock, fixing a race condition in FireWire core handling.

The patch adds new coexistence policy types, introduces rtw89_btc_set_policy/_v1 functions, moves policy setting into chip_ops, and updates chip operation tables for RTL8852A/C to use the appropriate function, enabling extra features for RTL8852C.
The patch deletes an unused assignment to the variable 'negative' in the ad2s1210 IIO driver, eliminating a dead‑store warning from clang scan‑build.

The patch modifies otx2_forward_vf_mbox_msgs to forward AF error codes to the VF by only treating -EIO as a communication failure, allowing other error codes to be passed through, fixing loss of error information.
The commit removes a conditional that rejected devices when the CHIP_IP_DISCOVERY flag was set, because IP‑based discovery support is now implemented, making the check obsolete.
Adds logic to enable/disable automatic GCP based on color depth and deep‑color support, writes the appropriate register bit, and defines the related constant.
The patch changes the IRQ entry assembly to stop using register R9, which is reserved for the task pointer, by moving FP and SP saves to R7 and R8 instead, preserving R9 across IRQ handling.
Adds support for VSC info‑packet revision 4 required by PSR‑SU, updating packet header bytes and handling logic, while keeping existing rev2 handling.
Updates tools/tracing/Makefile to add rtla to the default all, install and clean targets, defines new make rules for building, installing and cleaning rtla, and extends the .PHONY list accordingly.
Adds a compatible device entry for the PCA85073A RTC in the PCF85063 driver, enabling kernel recognition of this hardware via I2C and device tree identifiers.
The commit replaces the generic USB PD registration call with a Type‑C‑specific wrapper that passes the partner object as the parent, ensuring the PD object is linked to its Type‑C device.
Adds MMIO‑based MDIO‑mux nodes and related Ethernet PHY definitions to the ls1043a‑qds device tree, updates fpga node compatibility, and creates aliases for the new interfaces.
The patch moves VHT antenna pattern capability bits from sband init to stream init, ensuring TX/RX antenna pattern flags are set for 6 GHz operation, fixing a missing configuration bug.
Adds a gfp_t parameter to convert_context and updates its callers to pass GFP_ATOMIC in atomic contexts and GFP_KERNEL elsewhere, removing a BUG caused by sleeping in a spin‑locked section.

Adds a platform shutdown callback for the WCN6750 ath11k AHB device, splitting remove logic and ensuring DMA stops before the SMMU driver shuts down, preventing potential SMMU faults on system shutdown.
The commit adjusts ocelot_port_bridge_flags to map the NPI port to the CPU port index, allowing bridge port flag configuration on the NPI port for the Felix DSA driver.

Adds support for the qcom,msm8974-mss-pil compatible string in the MSM8916 MSS PIL DT binding, introducing the mss-supply property and conditional requirement, and removes obsolete references in q6v5.txt.
Adds a null‑pointer check for the OEM DDC service in dc_submit_i2c_oem; if ddc is NULL the function now returns false instead of dereferencing it, preventing crashes.

The commit removes the 'fsl,imx8qm-lpuart' entry from the compatible enum in the fsl-lpuart devicetree binding YAML because i.MX8QM is backward compatible with i.MX8QXP, forcing nodes to list both strings.

The patch moves the removal of a context's list link from context_close() to the release work handler, ensuring the list is modified only after the final reference is dropped and under the proper lock, fixing a GPF caused by premature removal. It also corrects spin_lock usage.

Implements a helper to allocate MSIX interrupt vectors for all virtqueues and config interrupt in the ifcvf vDPA driver, adding a new function ifcvf_alloc_vectors and integrating it into the IRQ request flow.
Removes an erroneous snd_BUG() in snd_usbmidi_output_open, returning -ENXIO when the port is NULL, thus preventing kernel panic on malformed USB MIDI devices.
Adds a guard so the probe call is only made when a separate probe address exists, preventing the 0x153 keyboard backlight from being turned off during driver initialization.

The patch changes the line‑buffer pixel depth selection: it now uses 36 bpp only on DCN display engines and falls back to 30 bpp for DCE versions, fixing dithering and broken pixel‑passthrough observed on DCE‑11.2 and earlier.
The patch renames a local variable in airtime.c from 'rate' to 'tx_rate' to avoid shadowing the outer 'rate' variable, and adds a 2021 Intel copyright line. No functional changes, only code clarity.

The patch replaces direct casts of literal addresses to pointers with the absolute_pointer() macro in boot code, adding temporary pointer variables and updating a cast in main.c, to avoid GCC 11/12 -Warray-bounds warnings.
The commit adds GPIO button and LED definitions for the Asus RTN-10U board and registers them in the board-specific switch, enabling support for its LEDs and buttons.

The patch removes a mutable irq_chip field, introduces a static immutable irq_chip structure, uses helper to set it, and updates IRQ handling code to use proper gpiolib helpers, addressing kernel warnings about mutable chips.

The commit modifies the device tree for imx8mp-phycore-som: it removes boot-on/always-on flags from LDO4 (unused) and adds them to LDO5 (required for SD‑Card VSEL), correcting the regulator configuration.

The patch replaces direct clock enable/disable calls with the driver’s suspend and resume helpers, adds a resume call during initialization, and removes clk_prepare_enable/disable handling, simplifying error paths.

The patch updates firmware‑path macros in intel_uc_fw.c to apply underscores uniformly within the macro concatenation, removing hard‑coded underscores from arguments and thus simplifying and standardising filename construction.
Adds a wrapper probe function and invokes snd_card_free_on_error to call snd_card_free() on probe failure, fixing the missing cleanup introduced by previous devres changes.
Adds support for the Apple Audio DMA Controller (ADMAC) by introducing Kconfig and Makefile entries and implementing a full DMA engine driver in drivers/dma/apple-admac.c.

The patch changes udl_handle_damage to take a drm_rect pointer, removes separate coordinate parameters, updates callers, and uses drm_rect helpers, simplifying the code without altering functionality.
Adds numerous handcrafted and generated structs and expected output sections to BPF selftests to verify btf_dump padding handling.
Adds a call to unregister_candev() in the error handling path of mcp251x_can_probe() so the CAN device is properly cleaned up when gpio setup fails.
Adjusts indentation of a bullet list line in Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-class-thermal to match style, removing a Sphinx warning about bullet list formatting.
Adds USB_1 over‑current detection to the Verdin i.MX8MP board by configuring the USB controller node as active‑low, defining a new pinctrl for the OC pin, and removing the previous GPIO hog mapping.

Adds support for CMD_ERROR_EVENT in the Kvaser USB leaf driver: defines command code, structs, error codes, updates size tables, and implements handling functions that log warnings/errors for various error conditions.

The patch renames ID_AA64ISAR2_EL1 field macros to include the _EL1 suffix, updating all references across asm, cpufeature, sysreg, KVM, and related code to follow the naming convention; no functional behavior changes.

The patch corrects egress rate‑limit configuration for CN10K devices by adding proper burst constants, handling device type in burst calculation, switching maxrate to 64‑bit, and building the correct register value for both OcteonTx2 and CN10K hardware.
The patch replaces a BUG_ON check with WARN_ON and adds a return, preventing a kernel panic and satisfying a checkpatch warning in efx_unregister_netdev.
Makes uid_strings static to avoid stack allocation, reducing code size and improving efficiency.
The patch removes the unused UsbTxAggDescNum member from struct hal_data_8188e, adds a macro USB_TXAGG_DESC_NUM = 0x6, and updates all code to use the macro instead of the struct field.
Updates uml_vector_default_bpf to accept a const pointer, adjusting both its definition and prototype to align with recent constification of MAC address handling in the UML vector driver.
Reworks testmode antenna mask handling in the mt7915 driver, replacing chainmask logic with antenna_mask, simplifying condition checks, removing chain‑shift adjustments, and adding mask validation.
The patch zeroes the page->private field when a page is split or migrated, keeping PG_private flag and private pointer consistent and fixing crashes seen in Ceph and other filesystems.
The patch fixes a misspelled word in a comment ("interrrupts" → "interrupts") in acp-pdm.c; it does not alter any executable code.
Adds missing PCS register and bit definitions to the Mediatek Ethernet driver header, updating macros to match discovered hardware details and improving code clarity.
Adds a warning when a framebuffer has no associated device, removes obsolete hot‑unplug workaround code, and updates the comment to reflect current expectations.

The commit removes per‑zone capacity handling, adds a single unusable_blocks_per_sec field, updates calculations to use it, and adds validation that all zones have the same capacity, aborting on mismatch.
Adds an SPDX-License-Identifier line to a documentation file and removes the old 'Licensed under GPLv2' text, updating the license reference to the SPDX identifier GPL-2.0-only.
The patch deletes the unused extern declaration of sni_cpu_time_init() from arch/mips/include/asm/sni.h because the function is no longer referenced anywhere.
The patch moves the call that programs the compbuf size to occur before the clock update in dcn20_optimize_bandwidth, fixing a P-State hang caused by the previous ordering.

Adds a pinctrl controller node to the MT6795 device tree, including compatible string, register ranges, interrupts, GPIO controller properties, and interrupt controller properties, enabling support for the pinctrl hardware.
The commit fixes numerous spelling mistakes in comments, strings, and documentation throughout the ath10k driver, as flagged by codespell, without altering any functional code.
The commit deletes unnecessary if‑checks before freeing IRQ and releasing memory in the driver remove routine, simplifying the code.
Updates KVM documentation to clarify MSR filtering behavior, rewords terminology, fixes an off‑by‑one description, and removes redundant text, without code changes.

The patch renames the swap‑flag accessor from page_swap_flags to folio_swap_flags, updates its implementation to accept a folio, and changes the sole caller in vmscan.c to use the new API, removing an unnecessary page‑to‑folio conversion.
The commit updates warning messages in mlx5e RSS code, replacing references to “LRO state” with the more generic term “packet merge state”, reflecting a naming change. No functional code is altered.
Implements nested VMLOAD/VMSAVE support in KVM's AMD SVM backend by adding a flag, capability handling, conditional intercept logic, and related helper functions.
The patch modifies cdns_fill_msg_resp to copy response data into msg->buf only for READ messages, leaving the buffer untouched for WRITE commands, thus preventing corruption of the caller's buffer.
The patch introduces a local variable 'dev' pointing to &pdev->dev and replaces direct uses of &pdev->dev throughout the probe function, reducing repetition and making the code cleaner.

Adds a struct to hold variables previously on the stack for dml32_CalculateSwathAndDETConfiguration, passes a pointer from callers, and updates the function to use struct fields, reducing stack usage.
The commit refactors the Chinese admin‑guide index documentation, converting plain indented lists into proper bullet list syntax for clearer formatting.
The commit moves the SVM TSC‑ratio constant definitions from svm.c into the public header svm.h, aligning the code with the SVM specification and centralising these macros.
Adds a new compatible string for the RZ/G2UL USB2 PHY in the devicetree binding documentation, enabling support for that SoC without driver changes.

The patch replaces OF‑specific property reads with the generic device‑property API, adds needed headers, updates allocation and parsing logic, and adjusts sensor creation functions to use fwnode handles, making the driver work on non‑OF platforms.
Adds two new device‑tree pinctrl nodes (dcmi_pins_c and dcmi_sleep_pins_c) defining an alternate pin multiplexing layout for DCMI pins, used on the AV96 board.
Reverts the earlier sbitmap batched wait_cnt accounting change that caused CPU stalls; restores the original sbitmap_queue_wake_up signature and related calls, undoing the regression.
The commit deletes the unused qid member from struct mt76_queue and removes all assignments to it in the mt76 driver, cleaning up dead code.
The patch reorders mmc_free_host to occur after register writes in moxart_remove(), preventing a use‑after‑free of the host structure that could be accessed via host->base.
Adds new_sta->sta.mlo = link_id >= 0; in ieee80211_prep_connection to correctly mark stations using MLO.

Adds minimal register set (regset) infrastructure for m68k, enabling core dump support in the ELF FDPIC loader by defining get function, regset descriptors, and view, compiled only when relevant configs are enabled.
Adds V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_MODIFY_LAYOUT to HFLIP and VFLIP controls so the driver correctly updates Bayer order when flips are applied, fixing incorrect layout handling.
Changes process_msg_close return type from int to void, removes always‑zero returns, updates caller to ignore return value; a pure code cleanup.

Implements the SBI v0.3 System Reset (SRST) extension for RISC‑V KVM guests by declaring the extension struct, adding it to the extension list, and providing a handler that maps SBI reset calls to KVM system reset or shutdown events.

Adds configurable function entry padding using -fpatchable-function-entry, introduces Kconfig options, propagates flags through Makefiles, updates assembly macros to emit NOP padding, and adjusts BPF dispatcher attributes to account for the padding.

The patch renames all occurrences of video_pll1 to video_pll across the i.MX8MN clock driver and its DT binding header, updating arrays, mux names, PLL identifiers, and related macros while preserving backward‑compatible constants.

The patch replaces the manual tracking of a single enabled CRTC in i9xx_update_wm() with the existing helper single_enabled_crtc(), removing the temporary 'enabled' variable and simplifying the logic.

The patch adds checks before disabling PSR and before using PSR state in static screen calculations, ensuring PSR panels are handled correctly when entering MALL mode and avoiding link overrides for phantom streams.
The patch changes audit_init_parent to take a const struct path pointer, adding a const qualifier to the parameter and preserving existing logic.
The patch modifies the tas2770 ASoC driver, changing channels_min from 2 to 1, thereby allowing mono playback streams for the mono speaker amp that can downmix and switch channels.
The patch replaces pm_runtime_get_sync calls with pm_runtime_resume_and_get in the STM32 VREFBUF regulator driver, removing extra error handling and simplifying power‑management code.

The patch updates the Intel raw NAND driver to read the chip‑select ('reg') from the NAND flash child node in the device tree, adds OF handling, and passes that node to nand_set_flash_node, fixing incorrect node usage.

The patch removes the XFS_IFORK_* macros and introduces inline helper functions (xfs_inode_fork_boff, xfs_inode_data_fork_size, etc.) that compute fork sizes with proper types, updating all call sites across the XFS codebase to use these functions.

The patch removes the LE‑specific HCI_OP_LE_READ_BUFFER_SIZE_V2 usage from hci_read_buffer_size_sync and adds it to hci_le_read_buffer_size_sync, ensuring the generic read uses the correct HCI_OP_READ_BUFFER_SIZE command.

The patch replaces a fixed-size stack array used for the efuse buffer with a dynamically allocated kmalloc buffer, adds error handling, and frees it with kfree, removing the need for __aligned(4) qualifier.
The patch changes several hubbub32 functions from external to static linkage, limiting them to dcn32_hubbub.c, removing missing‑prototype warnings and improving encapsulation.

The patch rewrites sysfs attribute group handling in the ptp_ocp driver: it builds a list of groups to register based on firmware capabilities, creates them with sysfs_create_groups, and removes them with sysfs_remove_groups, fixing crashes when detach tried to remove unregistered groups.
The patch deletes an unused function prototype intel_gt_create_kobj from intel_gt_sysfs.h, cleaning up dead code in the i915 driver.
Changes MAX9759 codec Kconfig to replace 'select GPIOLIB' with 'depends on GPIOLIB', making the GPIO dependency optional and removing spurious build warnings.
The commit replaces pagevec‑based LRU handling with folio_batch structures, adding functions like folio_batch_move_lru and adapting existing code to use the new batch API.

The patch removes the now‑unnecessary f2fs_lock_op/f2fs_unlock_op calls around f2fs_alloc_nid in f2fs_new_inode, as allocation no longer needs to block checkpoint and other locks already protect needed data.
Adds a new function perf_cpu_map__is_subset to determine if one CPU map is a subset of another, and declares it in the header, extending the lib/perf cpumap API.
Adds missing Linux kernel headers required by the Lynxpoint pinctrl driver and orders the include list alphabetically. No functional code changes, only compile‑time include adjustments.
The commit deletes the tcf_connmark_walker and tcf_connmark_search functions from act_connmark.c and uses the generic walk/search helpers instead, simplifying the code.

Adds support for 64‑bit software bundle initialization in the Nouveau GR engine, introduces sw_bundle64_init field, changes data types to u64, writes upper 32 bits when needed, and frees the new bundle64 allocation.

The patch replaces the old vb2_find_timestamp/index based buffer lookup with the newer vb2_find_buffer API, storing vb2_buffer pointers directly and simplifying reference handling in H264 and VP9 drivers.
Adds kernel unit tests for MCTP route input key/tag matching, defines FL_T macro, test structures, creates sockets and keys, and checks packet delivery under various configurations.
Adds a manual snd_card_free() call on probe error paths to correctly release resources, fixing a leak caused by earlier devres cleanup ordering.
The patch replaces an explicit dev_err call with the dev_err_probe helper in the mxsfb driver, simplifying error handling and adding a debugfs hint.

The patch replaces all uses of page->freelist with page->index in bootmem-related code, because freelist is intended for slab and index provides the same bits as an integer, eliminating pointer casts.

The patch updates the sdw-mockup driver to use the new snd_sdw_params_to_config helper for converting PCM hw_params to SoundWire stream and port configurations, removing manual assignments and adding the appropriate header.
Fixes a memory leak in configfs_create_dir and configfs_create_link by adding a missing configfs_put() on error paths to correct refcount handling.
The commit updates two return paths in XDP socket code, swapping ENOSPC for ENOMEM on allocation failure and ENOBUFS for a full Rx buffer, to give drivers clearer error information.
The patch removes the logic that unbinds the NVMe PCI driver after a reset failure and instead shuts down the controller, marking it dead, fixing abnormal driver removal behavior.
Adds `additionalProperties: false` to two devicetree binding YAML schemas, tightening validation to reject undocumented fields.
Adds free_uid(fpl->user) in __io_sqe_files_scm when no files are processed, releasing the UID reference before freeing the file list, fixing a memory leak in io_uring file registration.

Adds two 'select' statements (CRYPTO_AES and CRYPTO_CBC) to the CRYPTO_AES_ARM_BS Kconfig entry, ensuring required algorithms are enabled so the NEON‑based AES‑CBC implementation can register at boot.

The patch modifies the driver‑name setup helper to accept the card struct, uses the original name for formatting, adds a length check and logs an error when the driver name exceeds the allowed size, preventing driver‑name truncation issues.
Adds board configuration and ACPI match entries to support the adl_rt5682 platform, enabling the alc5682 headset codec without a speaker amplifier, following Intel BT offload design.

The patch removes the unused gfp_flags parameter from null_alloc_page in the null_blk driver, changes the function to take no arguments, and hard‑codes GFP_NOIO in the allocation calls; the sole caller is updated accordingly.

The commit introduces a sysfs-based user interface for DAMON, adding a Kconfig option, Makefile entry, and a large sysfs.c that creates hierarchical directories and attributes to configure virtual address monitoring.
Adds a NET dependency to INTEL_HFI_THERMAL in Kconfig to resolve a warning and subsequent build errors caused by missing NET support.

The patch corrects the bitmask constants in RX_DMA_GET_SPORT and RX_DMA_GET_SPORT_V2 macros, swapping the 0x7 and 0xf masks so the proper bits are extracted for source port values in the Mediatek Ethernet driver.
Resets two local flags inside the DCN3.2 prefetch calculation loop, fixing the loop's failure to exit when a prefetch attempt fails.

Adds mutex lock/unlock around roccat_report_event to serialize access to the circular buffer, eliminating a race that could free a report while roccat_read is copying it, thus fixing a use‑after‑free bug.

The patch removes all #if defined(CONFIG_DRM_AMD_DC_DCN) conditional blocks from the amdgpu_dm driver files, making the code unconditional because the DC layer is already OS‑agnostic. This cleans up redundant compile‑time configuration guards.

The patch stops clearing the DTIM period when the AP beacon is missing, ensuring the value set from beacon IEs is always stored in link->conf->dtim_period, and adjusts the handling of beacon IEs to correctly detect beacon presence.
Adds a list_for_each_table_entry macro and rewrites many ctl_table traversals in proc_sysctl.c to use it, simplifying loops and improving readability without altering functionality.
Patch modifies io_accept to handle multishot accept correctly when CQE overflow occurs, changing retry logic, setting result, and returning proper status, thereby fixing ordering issue.

The patch modifies mv88e6xxx_setup_port to fetch port capabilities via mv88e6xxx_get_caps, replacing reliance on uninitialized mac_capabilities, thereby correcting the default 10 Mbps speed on CPU/DSA ports.
The commit updates ath10k driver code to silence recent checkpatch warnings by replacing strlcpy with strscpy and fixing an unnecessary integer promotion in a printk format string.
Adds audio support to the ITE it66121 HDMI bridge devicetree binding by introducing the "#sound-dai-cells" property, enabling audio DAI description in device trees.
Adds a check in io_sendmsg_zc to reject zero‑copy sendmsg on sockets lacking ZC support, returning -EOPNOTSUPP, aligning behavior with other zerocopy operations.
Adds ethtool --identify support to the Netronome NFP driver by implementing a set_phys_id callback, exposing LED blink control, and adding the necessary kernel API and ABI handling.
The commit introduces a new Device Tree binding YAML file for the Himax hx83112b touchscreen controller and registers it in MAINTAINERS, enabling kernel support documentation for this hardware.
Adds a fixed regulator node, enables the second PCIe controller and its combphy, and defines related pinctrl and reset GPIOs in the quartz64-b device tree, providing hardware support for PCIe 2.

The patch renames nvme_kill_queues to nvme_mark_namespaces_dead, extracts the dead‑disk marking logic, and moves the queue unquiescing to callers via nvme_start_queues, updating all call sites and header declarations.

The patch removes CE (correctable error) checks from several UMC error‑address query functions, leaving only UE (uncorrectable error) checks, and deletes related comments. It simplifies logic and eliminates dead code across multiple hardware versions.

Adds missing extern for decrementer_max, includes mc146818rtc.h to define rtc_lock, removes duplicate rtc_lock extern, and moves dtl_consumer definition after asm/dtl.h include, eliminating sparse warnings in PowerPC time code.
Replace manual enable/disable string construction with str_enable_disable() helper and include its header, improving readability and reducing duplicated code in debug messages.

Adds conditional loading of xeCJK in kerneldoc-preamble.sty by checking for xeCJK.sty and the Noto CJK font, preventing LaTeX errors on systems lacking texlive-xecjk, and updates documentation notes accordingly.

The patch replaces all uses of struct sockaddr with struct sockaddr_storage in NFS client/server code, updating structs, function signatures, casts and memcpy calls so that address buffers match the larger storage size, eliminating false positive fortify_source overflow warnings.
The commit replaces INT_LIMIT(loff_t) with the clearer constant OFFSET_MAX in btrfs_wait_ordered_range, enhancing readability while keeping the same behavior.

The patch removes the obsolete of_gpio.h header, replaces of_* structures with the standard gpio_chip, updates the probe to use devm_gpiochip_add_data and ioremap, and adjusts related code, migrating the driver to the generic GPIO API.

The patch adds WGP‑mode detection, adjusts CU mask generation to use pairwise contiguous bits, and inserts a validation that CU masks are enabled in adjacent pairs on GFX10+ ASICs, correcting incorrect masking behavior.
The patch replaces manual delayed‑work handling with devm_delayed_work_autocancel, adds the needed header, removes the custom stop_irq_work helper, and simplifies the probe function.
Adds a hardware capability flag (HWCAP2_MTE3) for ARM64 asymmetric MTE mode, updating documentation, kernel headers, cpufeature table, and cpuinfo string to expose the feature to userspace.

The patch extracts all ICL combo‑PHY register definitions from i915_reg.h into a new header intel_combo_phy_regs.h, adds that header to the source files that need the registers, and removes the definitions from i915_reg.h. It reorganises code without altering runtime behavior.
The commit replaces manual OF match lookup with device_get_match_data() in the palmas driver, removing redundant code and simplifying the probe function.

The patch replaces manual 32‑bit reads of high/low registers with the kernel helper ioread64_hi_lo()/iowrite64_hi_lo(), adds the appropriate header, and removes redundant code, improving portability and readability of the PTP driver.
The commit deletes the Promise SATA SX8 block driver by removing its source file, Kconfig entry, and Makefile reference, effectively dropping support for this obsolete hardware.
The commit updates the devicetree binding documentation for Qualcomm USB VBUS regulators, renaming the example node from a generic 'dcdc' label to the more accurate 'usb-vbus-regulator' label.
Adds a Xen-specific error entry that includes UNTRAIN_RET and updates the alternative path to call it, ensuring proper unwind handling for Xen PV.
The commit deletes the obsolete <linux/gpio.h> include from drivers/media/i2c/ccs/ccs-core.c, leaving only the required <linux/gpio/consumer.h>, thus cleaning up unused code.
Adds linux/cyclades.h to the no-header-test list in usr/include/Makefile so the header_check test skips it, because the header is meant to emit a warning if included.

The commit introduces a dma_dev pointer in mt76_dev, initializes it, and replaces all dma_* calls to use this pointer, allowing the driver to override the device used for DMA mapping, needed for WED support.

The patch renames btrfs_insert_file_extent to btrfs_insert_hole_extent, removes unused parameters, updates all call sites, and sets hole‑extent fields to zero, simplifying the API for inserting hole extents.

The patch frees the debug_help_string buffer during module cleanup and releases the temporary 'new' buffer after constructing the help string, eliminating a kmemleak reported when loading and unloading the orangefs module.

The commit updates the Qualcomm ADSP remoteproc devicetree binding YAML to simplify interrupt definitions by replacing maxItems constraints with explicit item lists and adjusting conditional schema, improving documentation clarity.
The patch raises the GT reset watchdog timeout from 5 seconds to 60 seconds, giving resets more time to finish before the driver wedges the device, fixing the premature timeout issue.

Adds PTP interrupt support to the Sparx5 Ethernet driver: introduces ptp_irq field, obtains the IRQ from platform data, requests a threaded IRQ in start, implements a handler to process timestamp FIFO and deliver hardware timestamps.
Adds a requires_cpu flag to perf's evsel structure to distinguish uncore events that need a specific CPU, and updates propagation, parsing, cloning, and stat handling to use this flag.
Adds kernel-doc comments for two new fields in struct tegra_pmc, documenting core domain state synchronization and registration flags.
Adds a null‑pointer check after platform_get_resource() in the mt6397 RTC driver; returns -EINVAL when the resource is missing, preventing a dereference.
Renames the existing filter flow‑group identifiers to include “vlan” (macros, functions, struct members) for better readability and to separate them from the upcoming QinQ group.
The patch deletes the now‑unused declaration of arch_kprobe_override_function() from arch/x86/include/asm/kprobes.h, as the function was removed in a prior commit.
Adds a Kconfig option to test -mno-branch-likely support, moves the cc-option check to config time, and conditionally adds the flag in platform makefiles, removing clang warnings that become fatal.
The commit replaces of_irq_get_byname with fwnode_irq_get_byname in platform_get_irq_byname, allowing named IRQ retrieval for both OF and ACPI described devices via the fwnode abstraction.
Introduces a new helper hda_codec_device_remove() to encapsulate codec removal, updates hda.c to use it, and adds its prototype in hda.h, refactoring the removal path for better modularity.

The patch adds two new header files (`mmhub_3_0_1_offset.h` and `mmhub_3_0_1_sh_mask.h`) that define a comprehensive set of register offsets and bit‑field masks for the MMHUB block of AMD GPUs, specifically for version 3.0.1. No functional code changes are made; the commit simply expands the register database to support newer hardware revisions.
Replaces sprintf with snprintf in ptp_ocp_verify, adding buffer size to avoid overflow and make the code easier to review.

The patch refactors devm_clk_hw_register_clkdev() to use devm_add_action_or_reset instead of manual devres allocation and addition, removing extra code and simplifying error handling, without altering functionality.
The patch adds bounds checks for timestamp and command‑queue counter offsets in the Habana Labs driver, returning -EINVAL when offsets exceed the allocated buffer size.
Updates dev_warn call to use %#x instead of %d, correctly printing a u32 div_sel value and fixing misleading warning output.

Adds support for many additional TC flower filter keys in the Sparx5 driver (IS2 VCAP) and introduces a 128‑bit key API, implementing handlers for IPv4/IPv6, fragments, ports, VLAN, TCP flags, IP TOS, etc., enabling new filtering capabilities.
Adds driver support for Meson S4 SoCs by defining new registers, IRQ type handling, parameter struct, and compatible device entry.
Adds AMD PerfMonV2 CPU feature bit to cpufeatures.h and registers it in scattered.c, allowing the kernel to detect and use the new performance monitoring capabilities.
Fixes a 32‑byte memory leak in ibmvnic reset handling by freeing the rwi structure when the last reset in the list succeeds.
Adds an explicit cast of __fls to unsigned long to silence a format warning on arc, m68k and sparc, allowing the driver to compile without errors.

The patch renames the SR‑IOV helper file and header (ice_sriov.c/.h) to ice_vf_mbx.c/.h, updates the Makefile and include references, preparing the code for future Scalable IOV support. No functional changes are introduced.

The patch separates the inode's cp_task into cp_task (checkpoint I/O accounting) and a new wb_task (writeback context), adds a from_cp flag to f2fs_sync_dirty_inodes, updates callers, and uses wb_task to avoid deadlock and correct FS_CP_DATA_IO accounting when data_flush is enabled.

Adds a guard in ieee80211_tx_control_port to skip __ieee80211_select_queue when local->hw.queues is less than IEEE80211_NUM_ACS, preventing invalid queue IDs that caused transmission failures on devices such as rt2500-pci.

The commit introduces support for NVIDIA Tegra234 Multi‑Gigabit Ethernet (MGBE) in the stmmac driver stack: adds Kconfig option, Makefile entry, and a full platform driver implementation (probe, remove, suspend/resume, PHY handling).
Adds missing string representations for two driver states in iavf_state_str, enabling correct debug prints of state transitions.
Adds support for copying the kcore_dir (containing kallsyms, kcore, modules) from the input perf.data to the output during perf inject, introducing a new flag and copy routine.
Adds an allOf reference to the common can-controller.yaml in the sun4i-a10 CAN device tree binding, improving documentation consistency.
Moves the Renesas PRR devicetree binding file from the soc directory to the hwinfo directory, updates its $id URL, and adjusts the MAINTAINERS entry, reorganizing documentation.

The patch removes an explicit cast to u8 when comparing a u8 variable with macro VERSION_8190_BD in two driver files. Both operands are already u8, making the cast redundant. The change only edits source code and does not modify runtime behavior.
Deletes an unused #include <linux/msi.h> from drivers/iommu/of_iommu.c because the file does not reference any symbols from that header, eliminating unnecessary compilation dependency.

Adds support for NAND devices with OOB size >1 KB by introducing new BCH geometry calculations, a BBM‑in‑data‑chunk check, and an ecc_for_meta flag, enabling correct block‑mark placement for large OOB NAND.

The patch adds CONFIG_ARM64 && CONFIG_ENERGY_MODEL guards around Energy Model functions, provides fallback definitions, and removes unused static functions, eliminating -Werror=unused-function warnings and avoiding extra work when the Energy Model is disabled.

The patch initializes previously uninitialized variables, adds return‑value checks, and guards against dereferencing error pointers, addressing smatch static analysis warnings in rvu_npc_hash.c and otx2_dmac_flt.c.
The patch deletes a list of interrupt specifications that were incorrectly duplicated in the Exynos850 device‑tree, ensuring only the pin controller node defines wake‑up interrupts as required.
Adds config_intr and handle_interrupt callbacks to the KSZ9477 PHY driver, enabling interrupt handling like other Micrel PHYs.

Adds support for Apple DART2 IOMMU page table format used in M1 Pro/Max/Ultra, introducing new PTE masks, shift, protection bits, handling in address conversion functions, updating format enum and registration, and adjusting address size checks.
The patch adds an exception to checkpatch.pl so that macros expanding to a "case" statement are no longer flagged as errors, addressing false‑positive warnings for drivers that use case macros.
Replaces manual size calculation with struct_size() in pwc_decompress to avoid type errors and possible heap overflows, also silences a flexible‑array warning.
The patch replaces nodes_weight() with nodes_empty() in x86 NUMA initialization code, using a cheaper test for non‑empty node masks, improving efficiency without changing semantics.
Adds dma-channel-mask property and expands interrupts list in Tegra GPCDMA device tree nodes to correctly represent all 32 channels, fixing previous incorrect limitation.
Adds a WARN_ON check to the KVM_X86_OP macro, causing a warning when a required kvm_x86_ops function pointer is NULL during vendor module load, using corrected annotations.

The patch removes the generic vm_xsave_req_perm call from KVM self‑test utilities, moves it into the amx_test, and changes the function to accept a bit argument so tests can request different xsave bits.
The patch replaces clk_round_rate with rpi_firmware_clk_get_max_rate to correctly detect the hdmi_enable_4kp60 config flag after a clock subsystem change, ensuring proper 4k@60Hz HDMI output.

The commit makes the 'chip' argument mandatory for hwmon registration APIs, adds NULL checks for dev, name, and chip, and updates the kernel documentation to stop drivers from incorrectly converting old calls.
Replaces shift‑based flag definitions with the BIT macro and adds <linux/bits.h> for readability; no functional change.
Adds a function module_elf_check_arch that validates the ELF ABI level of a module against the kernel configuration, overriding the generic check for PowerPC64.

The commit rewrites the simpledrm driver to replace its simple‑KMS helpers with the generic DRM atomic helpers, introducing plane, CRTC and encoder objects and associated atomic check/update/disable functions, while keeping the driver behavior unchanged.

The commit replaces manual delayed work initialization and removal with devm_delayed_work_autocancel, eliminating the remove() function that cancelled uninitialized work, thus preventing invalid cancel calls.
Adds devlink_port_type_clear calls in error handling and cleanup paths to match earlier type_set, ensuring proper state cleanup for mlx4 devlink ports.

Adds a JPEG decode worker infrastructure to enable three decode hardware blocks to operate concurrently on MT8195. Implements hardware allocation, parameter setup, worker thread, new multithreaded m2m ops, variant registration, and supporting synchronization primitives.

Updates the cdce925 I2C clock driver to use the new simple probe API (probe_new) and i2c_match_id for device identification, removing the old probe signature that required an id argument, and adjusts the driver struct accordingly.

The patch replaces a manual delayed‑work cancellation implementation with the helper devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), adds the required header, and removes the custom cancel function and devm_add_action call, simplifying the driver.

Moves keep_towrite handling from ext4_writepage to ext4_bio_write_page, ensuring pages retain the TOWRITE tag when some buffers cannot be written, preventing writeback races that could cause data loss, especially during transaction commit.

The patch moves the retrieval of a devlink snapshot from devlink_nl_region_read_snapshot_fill to devlink_nl_cmd_region_read_dumpit, removes the unused attrs argument, and adds early validation of the snapshot ID, simplifying the code flow.
The patch increases the sleep delay from 5 to 15 seconds in two SELinux deprecation paths, making the deprecation messages more noticeable for users still using those knobs.
The commit updates the GS_MAX_INTF macro from 2 to 3 and adjusts the comment, enabling the driver to handle devices with up to three CAN‑FD channels, as some STM32G3 chips provide.
The patch deletes the unused integer variable 'found_devs' and its increment statements from the qla2xxx driver's local loop configuration function, eliminating dead code.

The patch deletes numerous VPRINTK() debug statements and the ata_scsi_dump_cdb helper, as the same information is already available via tracepoints, reducing unnecessary logging and dead code in the libata driver.
The patch corrects a kernel-doc comment in vmbus_drv.c, changing the documented function name to match the actual prototype, eliminating a compilation warning.

The patch replaces __iscsi_get_task with a new iscsi_get_task that safely increments the refcount only if non‑zero, removing the need to hold the session back_lock for most paths and adding fallback handling for the race where the task is being freed.

The patch replaces generic DRM debug prints with connector‑aware logging functions, passes drm_connector to helper functions, and consolidates tile debug output into a single line, without altering functional behavior.

The patch extracts the post‑power‑up handling from pci_power_up into a new helper pci_set_full_power_state, makes pci_power_up return a flag indicating whether BAR restoration is needed, and updates callers to use the new function, eliminating redundant work.

The patch removes ICL‑specific Thunderbolt power‑domain enum entries (POWER_DOMAIN_AUX_TBT_C…F) and replaces them with the generic TBT1‑4 names defined by the hardware spec, updating string conversion, power‑well tables and mappings accordingly.

The commit removes obsolete IDE driver documentation sections from Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst and updates a comment in pktcdvd.c to reference the correct SCSI driver path, cleaning up leftover references after the IDE driver was removed.

The patch adds a check for adev->enable_virtual_display to the condition that skips tiling‑flag validation, so when virtual display is active the driver no longer performs the FB modifier check, eliminating the warning seen on GFX9+ hardware.

The patch modifies ACPI_FLUSH_CPU_CACHE to call wbinvd only when not under a hypervisor, adding explanatory comments. This prevents the WBINVD instruction that causes a #VE exception in TDX guests, fixing the resulting failure.
The patch makes tcp_read_sock robust by handling cases where recv_actor returns a size larger than the remaining buffer, issuing a one‑time warning and capping the value to avoid infinite loops.
The patch replaces bh‑safe locking in rhashtable with irq‑safe locking, adding flag handling and using local_irq_save/restore, thus enabling rhashtable usage from interrupt contexts.
Adds an explicit check that the requested length does not exceed the proxy buffer size, preventing possible out‑of‑bounds writes and silencing a GCC array‑bounds warning.

The patch replaces manual dev_pm_ops definition with DEFINE_RUNTIME_DEV_PM_OPS macro and uses pm_ptr to reference it, removing __maybe_unused attributes and allowing the compiler to drop the structure when CONFIG_PM is disabled.
Adds <linux/kstrtox.h> to several RTC driver files because kstrto* functions moved from kernel.h, restoring correct compilation.

The patch modifies sdma_v5_2_hw_fini to avoid early return on SR‑IOV VFs, disables SDMA, then re‑enables it and its context switch when under SR‑IOV, clearing the DRM entity and fixing resume failures.
Adds a delayed‑work timeout mechanism for the Mediatek JPEG decoder, introducing new struct fields and initializing the work in probe, plus handling cancellation on IRQ.

Adds support for entering zstate (low‑power) during extended vblank periods obtained from FreeSync. Introduces caps, debug options, stream update flags, timing adjustments, hardware programming, and DML calculations to decide and apply the optimization.
Deletes the &ipa_fw_mem node from the sc7180‑trogdor device‑tree to stop a reserved‑memory overlap that triggers a boot‑time error message.
The patch replaces direct rb_prev/rb_next calls in merge_state with the helper functions prev_state/next_state, removing duplicated code and simplifying the logic while preserving existing behavior.

The patch updates the hqd_destroy callback prototype in kgd_kfd_interface.h, changing the reset_type parameter from uint32_t to enum kfd_preempt_type, aligning it with actual implementations and eliminating a CFI type mismatch that caused a kernel crash on Clang-built kernels.

The commit changes the device‑tree for the Meson SM1 Odroid board, switching the tf_io regulator enable‑gpio from active‑high to open‑drain, which resolves a boot‑loop after reboot caused by the wrong GPIO configuration.
Consolidates duplicated logic for handling parent marks that do not watch children, ensuring consistent event handling and correcting previous incorrect ignore‑mask and reporting behavior.

Adds support for multiple BAR mapping schemes in the EPF NTB driver by introducing a configurable mw_bar field, handling optional peer scratchpad BAR, and adding device-specific data (e.g., mx8) to select BAR numbers, thus enabling new hardware configurations.
The commit updates the STM32 pinctrl devicetree binding YAML: renames the property from 'reset' to the correct 'resets' and adds 'additionalProperties: false' to enforce strict validation.
The patch adds propagation of socket timestamp flags to the IPv6 ping implementation, enabling ping6 to report timestamps when requested.
Adds a new compatible string for the Microchip icicle reference design in the RISC‑V devicetree binding documentation, documenting the FPGA fabric version.

The patch adds error‑path handling in rio_register_mport(): on device_register failure it logs, removes the port from the global list, and calls put_device to release the reference so the allocated name is freed during kobject_cleanup().

The commit separates kernel‑only capability flags from the user‑visible device_cap_flags by introducing a new kernel_cap_flags bitmap, updates all drivers and core code to use the appropriate flag set, adds comments and removes unused kernel flags, improving code clarity and correctness.
The commit adds conditional compiler flags to the ath9k Makefile to suppress a spurious -Warray-bounds warning from GCC 12, without changing driver functionality.
Adds a check in KVM CPUID handling to clear the XFD bit for each state component when the XFD base feature is absent, ensuring compliance with Intel's XFD spec.

Adds explicit #include <linux/highmem.h> and <linux/swap.h> in several i915 driver files and removes an unnecessary <linux/i2c.h> include from i915_drv.h, tightening header dependencies and improving compilation correctness.
Adds a flag MLX5_ESWITCH_VPORT_ACL_NS_CREATED to track ACL namespace creation, skips reinitialization on mode switches, and clears the flag on cleanup, preventing unnecessary allocation/free cycles.

Adds an external_power_changed callback for BQ25892 that reads the USB_TYPE from the supplier power supply and sets the input current limit accordingly, integrating external charger detection into the driver.
The patch replaces all uses of SERIAL_XMIT_SIZE with UART_XMIT_SIZE in several tty drivers and removes the old SERIAL_XMIT_SIZE definition, adding the appropriate header for UART_XMIT_SIZE.

The patch refactors the KVM xapic_ipi_test self‑test to stop using numeric vCPU IDs and instead pass around struct kvm_vcpu pointers, updating thread parameters, helper functions, and VM creation calls accordingly.

The patch extracts duplicated NAT handling code from OVS and TC, places it in a new netfilter file nf_nat_ovs.c, exports nf_ct_nat, updates Kconfig, Makefile, and modifies OVS conntrack and TC act_ct to call the shared function, removing duplicated implementations.
Removes inclusion of da7219-aad.h and direct call to da7219_aad_jack_det(), replacing it with snd_soc_component_set_jack() to use the proper public API for jack detection.
The patch deletes four now‑unused AVIC function prototypes from svm.h, which were left after converting calls to static inline functions. No code behavior changes; only header cleanup.
